guitar.guitaristsText: John Lennon / George Harrison / Paul McCartney
guitar.modelsText: Rickenbacker 325/360-12, Gretsch, Epiphone Casino, Gibson J-160E
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: well documented across multiple guitars and eras — Lennon's Rickenbacker 325/Casino, Harrison's Gretsch/Rickenbacker 360-12, McCartney mainly bass (Hofner) with some guitar use.
guitar.notes: Original entry reasonable as a summary across three members and many guitars; kept as-is.

tone.target: 1965 studio acoustic ballad, no electric guitar
tone.profile: 1965 studio acoustic ballad, no electric guitar
tone.summary: A highly clean signal chain utilizing a flat pre-amp (Comp) into a low-gain US Deluxe model with a clear IR, emphasizing natural room ambience and fingerpicked transients.
corrections: use acoustic sim or flat DI tone

blocks.purpose: Clean up any unwanted hum or noise from the electric guitar input.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for clean tones.

blocks.purpose: Smooth out the dynamics and enhance the transient clarity required for fingerpicked acoustic playing.
blocks.gap: The Comp module is used to simulate the gentle compression of a studio microphone setup, enhancing sustain without adding grit.

blocks.purpose: Maintain a completely clean signal path; no drive or breakup is allowed.
blocks.gap: N/A. Using the 'None' module to ensure zero gain stage coloration.

blocks.purpose: Provide a clean, articulate, and non-colored tone suitable for acoustic simulation without sounding like an electric amp.
blocks.gap: The US Deluxe is the cleanest available model. We must keep gain extremely low to avoid any perceived 'electric' character.

blocks.purpose: Simulate a close studio microphone recording setup (DI) with minimal cabinet coloration.
blocks.gap: While an acoustic sim would be ideal, the US 2x12 provides the flattest and most open soundboard simulation available in the catalog.

blocks.purpose: Slightly boost the upper mids and highs to enhance string articulation and clarity (transients).
blocks.gap: Used for surgical tone shaping, compensating for potential muddiness in the signal chain.

blocks.purpose: Provide a minimal, natural room ambience to place the sound in a studio environment without sounding like an echo.
blocks.gap: The reverb must be kept very low (20% mix) and decay time moderate to avoid washing out the delicate fingerpicking transients.

blocks.purpose: Final output level adjustment to match the required studio recording volume.

improvements.summary: Replace generic IR with a flat, close-mic acoustic simulation IR for maximum transient clarity.

proposals.reason: The US 2x12 is too 'electric' sounding; need a pure DI/acoustic IR for studio fidelity.
